translation.title: Diclofenac Diethylammonium Gel
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and reduction of inflammation in traumatic inflammation of tendons, ligaments, muscles and joints (such as sprains and bruises), localized forms of soft-tissue rheumatism (such as tendovaginitis, shoulder-hand syndrome, bursitis and periarthritis), and localized forms of rheumatic disease (such as osteoarthrosis of the peripheral joints and spine).
translation.usage: Adults and adolescents 12 years and older: depending on the size of the painful area, apply 2 to 4 g at a time to the affected area 3 to 4 times a day and rub it in gently.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it or have been in the past, if you are or have been hypersensitive to aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics with reactions such as asthma attacks, hives or acute rhinitis, for children 12 years old or younger, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are elderly, or if you are or have been hypersensitive to propylene glycol. Do not use it on skin with lesions (bleeding skin disorders, eczema, infected lesions, burns or wounds), or in the eyes or on mucous membranes. Wash your hands thoroughly after use (except when applying it to finger joints). Using it over a large area for a long time can cause systemic (whole-body) adverse reactions. Do not use an occlusive (airtight) dressing over it. If you are taking loop diuretics (such as furosemide), thiazide diuretics, medicines that interfere with blood clotting (such as warfarin), antiplatelet medicines (such as aspirin), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Adverse reactions may occur - occasionally rash, eczema, erythema (red patches) and dermatitis (including contact dermatitis), rarely blistering dermatitis, and very rarely hypersensitivity reactions, angioneurotic edema (swelling), asthma, photosensitivity reactions or pustular rash; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis, or serious gastrointestinal reactions including bleeding, ulcer or perforation of the stomach or intestines occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Using it on damaged skin can cause temporary irritation and a tingling sensation, so use it with care. Store below 30 degrees Celsius.
